C-62.Name: Per-diagram appearance: Auto, Custom, Light and Dark
C-62.Summary: Implement the reviewed mock: an appearance button beside expand on Mermaid/Pele diagrams and in the fullscreen viewer, with four radio-menu modes and immediate, isolated recoloring. Bridge author Mermaid themeVariables to Pele colors without restoring the Mermaid engine.
C-62.Problem: Pele intentionally ignores Mermaid themes/themeVariables. Mark currently exposes only document-wide theming; a diagram cannot retain a light/dark or author palette independently.

Goals.R-1: Auto follows the document, Custom uses supported author color variables and inline styles, and Light/Dark use fixed readable palettes. Custom is disabled without a usable author palette. Opening/dismissing the menu changes no content.
Goals.R-2: Writable documents store the selection in a namespaced Mermaid comment, %% mark:appearance MODE %%, inside the fence after any YAML frontmatter. Only that metadata changes; author settings, comments and diagram source survive. A choice is one undoable edit; selecting the existing mode is a no-op.
Goals.R-3: Read-only/locked and Split View mirror surfaces allow temporary view-only choices, explicitly labeled in the menu, without document/history/save mutations. Writable choices remain portable in the Markdown; unsupported/invalid modes safely resolve to Auto.
Goals.R-4: Read author colors from YAML config.themeVariables and init directives using a bounded safe parser. Map supported semantic colors and series colors to local Pele CSS variables; accept only literal hex colors. Forced Light/Dark normalize inline color overrides in the displayed SVG while preserving source and non-color styling. Auto retains the existing classDef behavior.
Goals.R-5: Editor, fullscreen clone and standalone HTML export use the same appearance policy, including read-only preview overrides. The viewer keeps pan/zoom during a choice. Global theme switches recolor Auto while fixed/custom diagrams retain their palette. Appearance-only choices reuse the raw SVG cache.
Goals.R-6: Menu supports mouse, touch and keyboard, radio state, focus restoration, disabled Custom explanation, viewport clamping, outside dismissal and Esc-before-viewer handling. Removed/replaced blocks, source changes, teardown and pending render races cannot mutate another block or leak listeners.

Constraints.Item: Preserve pre-existing C-57/C-60 dirty work and unrelated active bundles; execute sequentially.
No packaged app build, release, publication or installed-app replacement in this change.
Use yaml 2.8.3, already installed transitively, as an explicit dependency; retain bounded parsing and avoid private Pele imports.

NonGoals.Item: No palette editor, automatic source conversion to SVG, geometry compatibility with Mermaid, font/layout theme compatibility, or exact reproduction of every Mermaid themeVariable. Other diagram engines and tables keep existing controls.

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: Pure policy tests cover malformed/bounded metadata, frontmatter/init colors, comment-preserving writes, duplicates/unknown modes, inline normalization and fixed palette independence.
Real Muya/menu tests cover history, selection, isolated blocks, read-only, keyboard, stale blocks, teardown and viewer synchronization; export tests assert identical local policy.

Chromium and WebKit browser checks cover four modes, computed colors, global theme changes, reload/source persistence, undo, viewer focus/zoom and narrow menus. Full renderer suite and frontend build pass; source/GRACE review findings are resolved or reported.

VerificationIntent.ExpectedEvidence: Fresh policy/menu/export assertions, browser computed-color/focus checks, review and selected GRACE gate evidence; unrelated C-55 stale assertions remain explicitly separated.

C-62.Approval: User approved the four-mode mock and instructed «выглядит прикольно, шгрейс углы, корнеры, ревью, тесты и го». This authorizes implementation and routine engineering choices within this feature, including sequential execution and fixes identified by review.
